title: Grade 3 Science — Daily Weather and Long-Term Climate
subject: Science
description: Practice with questions on temperature, precipitation, graphs, observations.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Which describes weather?
Which describes climate?
choices: This town usually has rainy springs.

questions.question: What instrument measures air temperature?
Which tool measures how much it rained?
Which tool can show the direction the wind comes from?
What evidence best describes a city's climate?
Which is a form of precipitation?
A chart shows five sunny days in a row. What can you conclude?
choices: It was sunny each of those five days.
It will always be sunny there.
It never rains in the town.

questions.question: Why might two towns have different weather on the same day?
choices: They both use the same clock.

questions.question: A place is usually dry. It rained hard today. Which could both be true?
choices: A rainy day means its climate is always wet.
Its climate is dry and its weather was rainy today.
The rain changed every past day.
A dry climate can never get rain.

questions.question: Which measurement helps show which town was colder at noon today?
choices: each town's distance from a river
each town's total daylight last year

questions.question: What does a weather forecast tell?
choices: which clouds were visible 100 years ago
how many roads a town has

questions.question: Which record supports a claim about long-term snowfall?
Three days had high temperatures of 21°C, 19°C, and 24°C. Which was warmest?
Which is shown on a graph of rain totals by month?
choices: the amount of rain in each month

questions.question: Clouds cover the park today, though the park has many sunny days most years. What does cloudy describe?
What can a wind speed reading help you tell?
Which example compares climates?
choices: The morning was cloudy and lunch was sunny.
Town A usually has colder winters than Town B.

questions.question: A student wants to measure outdoor air temperature fairly each day. What should stay the same?
A forecast shows possible rain. Which plan fits the information?
choices: Assume it will rain at one exact minute.
Expect snow every day next year.
Bring a raincoat in case it rains.
